Question 1
?

Let a=⟨2,3,0⟩ and b=⟨6,4,0⟩. Find a×b.

a
⟨0,0,6⟩
b
⟨10,0,0⟩
c
⟨0,−10,0⟩
d
⟨−10,0,10⟩
e
⟨0,0,−10⟩
Submit

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Using the determinant formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\times b & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(3\cdot 0-4\cdot 0)i-(2\cdot 0-6\cdot 0)j+(2\cdot 4-6\cdot 3)k \\  & =(0)i-(0)j+(8-18)k \\  & =⟨0,0,-10⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

b
 x=2
c
 x=1
d
 x=±1
e
 x=−1,2

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Using the determinant formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\times b & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 2x\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 1 & 2x\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -1 & 2x\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0+4)i-(4x-4)j+(2-0)k \\  & =⟨4,-4x+4,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the magnitude, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,a\times b\,| & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-4x+4)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+16{x}^{2}-32x+16+4} \\  & =\sqrt{16{x}^{2}-32x+36}.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, we solve for $x$ the following equation:

$$
